title: UFO Over Tehran Sparks Theories About Secret US Aircraft and Iranian Weapons
site_name: ColombiaOne: News from Colombia and the World
excerpt: Viral images of a UFO over Tehran sparked speculation ranging from commercial drones to classified military reconnaissance platforms.
content:
Videos reportedly recorded over Tehran on Sept. 20 show an unidentified object with blue, white, pink and yellow lights, sparking speculation online about whether it could be a drone, LED-equipped kite, aircraft or military surveillance platform. The footage has not established the object’s identity, size, altitude or distance from the camera.

Videos circulating online reportedly show the object near Tehran’s Azadegan Expressway at about 7:30 p.m. The footage depicts several bright lights arranged in a curved or semicircular formation against the night sky. In some clips, the lights appear to hover or move slowly. One person who posted a video said the object appeared near clouds and made no audible sound. These details come from the people who posted the footage and have not been independently verified.

The lack of reliable reference points makes the footage difficult to interpret. Without fixed landmarks or objects of known size, viewers cannot determine how large the object was, how far away it was, how high it was flying or how quickly it was moving. Iranian authorities have not publicly identified the object or announced that it posed a threat.

The footage shows lights, but little else

The most consistent visual feature is the object’s lighting. Rather than showing a clearly identifiable aircraft, the footage shows a cluster of colored lights that appears to form a broad, curved shape.

The darkness also makes it difficult to establish the object’s physical structure. Without a fixed reference point in the frame, the footage cannot show whether the lights belonged to a large object at a distance or a smaller object closer to the camera.

The same limitation applies to the apparent hovering. Shaky, low-resolution footage can make an object appear stationary or move differently from its actual flight path when there are no nearby structures or other reference points.

The term UFO, or unidentified flying object, does not itself indicate extraterrestrial technology. It simply means the object has not been identified.

A kite or drone could explain the lights

One of the simpler explanations circulating online is that the object was an LED-equipped kite. Viewed from the ground at night, such a kite could appear as a cluster of lights while its frame and tether remain difficult to see.

Another possibility is a drone or multiple drones flying together. Other explanations raised online include conventional aircraft and military surveillance equipment. None of these possibilities has been confirmed.

Al Jazeera and other media reports have similarly described speculation ranging from a kite or drone to more advanced military technology. The available footage does not provide enough information to establish which explanation, if any, is correct.

War has turned the sighting into a military mystery

The timing has added to speculation because the footage emerged amid heightened tensions between Iran and the United States.

On Sept. 21, Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps spokesman Brig. Gen. Hossein Mohebbi warned that Iran would introduce “new weapons with new capabilities” if the United States launched another attack and said the world would be surprised by them. He also said Iran had new targets that had not previously been attacked.

Mohebbi’s comments concerned Iran’s response to a possible renewed U.S. attack and did not refer to the object seen in the Tehran videos. There is no public confirmation from Iranian military or civilian aviation authorities that the footage showed a weapons test or military operation.

Social media posts have nevertheless suggested that the object could have been a reconnaissance drone or an Iranian defense prototype.

The U.S. “Black Manta” theory remains unconfirmed

Another theory circulating online suggests that the object could be an advanced U.S. surveillance aircraft. Posts have revived the long-running story of the TR-3B “Black Manta,” supposedly a highly classified triangular U.S. aircraft with unusual flight capabilities.

The U.S. government has not publicly confirmed the existence of an aircraft called the TR-3B Black Manta. The available Tehran footage also does not clearly show a triangular aircraft or provide other evidence connecting the sighting to the alleged platform.

The theory therefore remains speculation rather than an established explanation for the footage.

A 50-year-old Tehran UFO case adds another layer

The new videos appeared almost 50 years after one of the most well-known UFO incidents associated with Iran.

On Sept. 19, 1976, residents of Tehran reported seeing a bright object over the city, prompting the Iranian military to dispatch F-4 fighter jets to investigate. Declassified U.S. government records preserved by the National Security Agency document the incident, including reports from U.S. military and diplomatic officials.

One declassified report described the object as brighter and larger than an ordinary star. It also recorded an Iranian pilot reporting problems with his aircraft’s instrumentation and communications during the attempted interception.

The 1976 incident is documented in government records, but there is no evidence connecting it to the Sept. 20, 2026 videos. The proximity of the dates has nevertheless become part of the online discussion surrounding the latest footage.

What can actually be established

The available evidence establishes that videos circulated online showing an unidentified cluster of colored lights reportedly seen over Tehran on the night of Sept. 20. One widely circulated recording is reportedly associated with the Azadegan Expressway and a time of about 7:30 p.m., but those details have not been independently verified.

The footage does not establish the object’s physical dimensions, altitude, distance, speed or identity. Iranian authorities have not publicly identified it.

A kite, drone, aircraft or military platform could potentially account for some of the observed features, but none has been confirmed. The “Black Manta” theory and claims that Iran was testing a new weapon likewise remain unverified.

For now, the most accurate description is an unidentified aerial sighting that has generated multiple explanations, with insufficient evidence to determine what was captured on camera.
